items.note: Mōdāsā grant dated V.S. 1067 (6 May 1011 A.C.) introduces four Paramāra rulers: Siyaka, Vākpatirāja, Sindhurāja, and Bhōjadēva.
Land grant of two halas of land for growing kōdrava, mudga, vṛhi (paddy) and tila (sesamum), including corn in the threshing floor adjoining the houses.
Procedure of the grant: land examined by representatives of Brāhmaṇas, shown to the donee, then given in the presence of named witnesses; evidence for how land grants were executed.
Editor suggests the Chālukya prince Vatsarāja may have been a feudatory of Bhōja, who was then aggrandising himself at the cost of his enemy the Chaulukya Mūlarāja.

items.note: Mahaudī grant: Bhōjadēva, successor of Sindhurājadēva, who succeeded Vākpatirājadēva, who succeeded Siyakadēva.
Donation on the full-moon day of Śrāvaṇa, year 1074, equated with 30 July 1018 A.C.
The Mahaudī charter is the first Paramāra grant in the Bhopāl territory, showing this region was in Bhōja's kingdom before 1018 A.C.
King at Dhārā orders the villagers to render the donee all taxes in cash, share of crop produce, periodical offerings, additional taxes and dues.
Dhārā of the inscription is Dhār, 'the Paramāra capital' and now headquarters of the Dhār District.
